examples.en: I feel a sense of distance toward people I have just met.

examples.ko: 그 일 이후로 친구와 거리감이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Since that incident, a distance has grown between my friend and me.

examples.ko: 사진 속 건물은 거리감이 잘 안 느껴져요.
examples.en: I can't get a good sense of distance from the building in the photo.
The teacher gets along with students without any distance.

examples.ko: 거리감을 좁히려고 내가 먼저 말을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I spoke first to close the distance.
When driving, judging the distance to the car ahead is important.

explain: '거리감'은 마음의 거리와 눈으로 보는 거리에 모두 써요. 사람 사이에서는 '거리감이 느껴지다', '거리감이 생기다', '거리감을 좁히다'가 자주 짝이 돼요. 반대로 가깝게 느끼는 마음은 '친밀감'이에요.

phrases.en: We narrowed the distance between us by eating together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이를 더 가깝게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means making people feel closer to each other.

phrases.en: That teacher has no distance from the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 편하고 가까운 사이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say people are comfortable and close with each other.

phrases.en: At the new school, I felt distant from the other students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느껴지다'와 달리 내가 느낀다는 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '느껴지다', this makes it clear that I am the one who feels it.

explain_en: 거리감 is used both for emotional distance and for distance judged by the eye. Between people it often pairs as 거리감이 느껴지다, 거리감이 생기다 and 거리감을 좁히다. The opposite feeling of closeness is 친밀감.

examples.ko: 거대한 산을 보니 저절로 경외심이 들었어요.
examples.en: Seeing the huge mountain, I naturally felt a sense of awe.
People in the past lived with awe toward nature.
I even felt awe at my teacher's long years of effort.

examples.ko: 그의 연주에는 경외심을 불러일으키는 힘이 있어요.
examples.en: His performance has a power that inspires awe.

examples.ko: 경외심 없이 자연을 마구 대하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat nature carelessly without a sense of awe.

examples.ko: 아이는 큰 고래를 보고 경외심 섞인 눈으로 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The child saw the huge whale and stared with eyes full of awe.

explain: '경외심을 느끼다/가지다/불러일으키다'로 자주 써요. '존경심'은 보통 사람에게 쓰고, '경외심'은 자연이나 위대한 존재처럼 크고 놀라운 것에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 별이 가득한 밤하늘을 보며 경외심을 느꼈어요.
phrases.en: I felt awe looking at the night sky full of stars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 놀라운 것 앞에서 마음속에 생기는 느낌을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you feel awe in front of something great and amazing.

phrases.example: 웅장한 성당은 보는 사람에게 경외심을 불러일으켜요.
phrases.en: The grand cathedral inspires awe in those who see it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 대상이 사람들에게 경외심을 생기게 할 때 써서, 느끼는 사람이 아니라 대상이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here the thing itself is the subject and it causes awe in others.

phrases.example: 큰 폭포 앞에 서니 경외심이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: Standing in front of the huge waterfall, I felt a sense of awe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느끼다'보다 어떤 장면을 보고 저절로 마음이 생겼다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 느끼다, it stresses that the feeling arose by itself on seeing something.

explain_en: It is often used as '경외심을 느끼다', '가지다' or '불러일으키다'. '존경심' is usually for people, while '경외심' suits grand, impressive things such as nature or something great.

examples.en: You must not treat the two incidents as the same.
Please don't lump me together with that person.
Many people equate happiness with money.
The audience identified themselves with the hero.
It is rude to treat the two countries as the same.
I equate success with work, so I can't rest.

explain: 'A를 B와 동일시하다'처럼 목적어 하나와 '와/과' 말이 같이 와요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보이고, 말로는 '똑같이 보다', '같게 보다'가 쉬워요. 차이를 보는 '비교하다'와는 방향이 반대예요.

phrases.example: 두 말은 뜻이 달라서 동일시할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: The two words have different meanings, so they can't be equated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 수 없다'를 붙여 같게 볼 수 없다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-l su eopda', it says two things cannot be treated as the same.

phrases.example: 두 사람을 똑같이 보면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't see the two people as the same.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동일시하다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say 'dongilsihada'.

phrases.example: 영화를 볼 때 주인공과 자신을 동일시했어요.
phrases.en: While watching the movie, I identified myself with the main character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이나 인물에 자기를 겹쳐 생각할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you see yourself in another person or character.

explain_en: It takes an object plus a 와/과 phrase, as in 'A를 B와 동일시하다'. It is common in news and writing, while in speech '똑같이 보다' or '같게 보다' are easier. It points the opposite way from 비교하다, which looks for differences.

en: to have an ambition; to have an interest

examples.ko: 뜻있는 사람들이 모여 마을 도서관을 만들었어요.
examples.en: Public-spirited people gathered and built a village library.
I donated money to be used for a worthy cause.

examples.ko: 저도 뜻있는 일을 함께 해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I also want to do something meaningful together.
The school was built with help from well-meaning people.

examples.ko: 뜻있게 시간을 쓰고 싶어서 봉사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started volunteering because I wanted to spend my time meaningfully.
Friends with shared goals got together and formed a club.

explain: '뜻있는 사람들'처럼 좋은 뜻을 품은 사람에게 많이 써요. '뜻깊다'는 일이나 날 자체의 의미가 클 때 주로 쓰고, '뜻있다'는 그런 마음을 가진 사람이나 일을 꾸밀 때 자주 나와요. 보통 '뜻있는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.

phrases.example: 저는 아이들을 돕는 뜻있는 일을 하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to do meaningful work helping children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 목적이 있는 일을 가리킬 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for work done for a good purpose.

phrases.en: Today I went to a meaningful gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 뜻으로 모인 모임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a gathering with a good purpose.

phrases.example: 뜻있는 사람들이 모여 함께 봉사를 해요.
phrases.en: Well-intentioned people gather and do volunteer work together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 뜻을 품은 사람들을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for people who hold good intentions.

explain_en: It is often used for people with good intentions, as in '뜻있는 사람들'. '뜻깊다' is mainly for an event or day that holds great meaning, while '뜻있다' often describes people or deeds with that spirit. It usually appears as '뜻있는' before a noun.

examples.en: Animals also have a strong maternal instinct to protect their young.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 모성을 주제로 한 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is a story about motherhood.

examples.ko: 아이가 아프면 모성이 더 강해진다고들 말해요.
examples.en: People say a mother's instinct gets stronger when her child is sick.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 모성과 직업 사이의 갈등을 그려요.
examples.en: This drama portrays the conflict between motherhood and a career.

examples.ko: 모성 보호 제도가 있어서 출산 휴가를 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: There is a maternity protection system, so you can take maternity leave.
It is a photo that shows a mother bear's maternal love.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '부성'이고, 보통 '모성애'라는 형태로 더 자주 들려요. '모성 보호'처럼 제도나 뉴스에서도 쓰이니 '엄마의 마음' 같은 일상적인 말과 구별해서 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: A mother's maternal love is truly deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모성'보다 더 자주 쓰고, 어머니가 자식에게 갖는 사랑을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often than 모성, meaning a mother's love for her child.

phrases.en: The company runs a maternity protection program.
phrases.nuance_ko: 임신이나 출산을 한 여성을 지키는 제도나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in policies and news about protecting women who are pregnant or have given birth.

phrases.en: Cats have a strong maternal instinct for caring for their young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어미가 새끼를 지키려는 마음이 클 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a mother strongly wants to protect her young.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a strong maternal instinct

explain_en: Its counterpart is '부성' (paternal instinct), and you will often hear it as '모성애'. It also appears in institutional or news phrases like '모성 보호' (maternity protection), so keep it separate from everyday expressions like '엄마의 마음'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말과 행동이 자주 모순돼요.
examples.en: His words and actions often contradict each other.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 설명이 서로 모순되어서 이상했어요.
examples.en: The two accounts contradicted each other, which was strange.

examples.ko: 모순되는 내용이 한 글에 같이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Contradictory content is in the same text.

examples.ko: 결과가 처음 계획과 모순되지 않아서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad the result does not conflict with the original plan.

examples.ko: 건강을 챙기면서 밤을 새우는 건 모순된 행동이에요.
examples.en: Looking after your health while staying up all night is contradictory behavior.

examples.ko: 앞뒤가 모순될 때는 다시 확인해 봐요.
examples.en: When the beginning and the end contradict each other, check again.

explain: 말, 생각, 행동이 서로 맞지 않을 때 써요. '모순이 있다', '모순이 생기다'처럼 명사 '모순'도 많이 써요. 따로 보면 맞아 보이는데 같이 놓으면 안 맞는다는 느낌이고, '앞뒤가 안 맞다'로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 이야기를 듣다 보니 앞뒤에 모순이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: As I listened, a contradiction appeared in the story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사 '모순'을 써서 모순이 나타났다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 모순 to say that a contradiction has appeared.

phrases.example: 그 사람 말은 앞뒤가 안 맞아요.
phrases.en: What he says doesn't add up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모순되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more common in everyday speech than 모순되다.

phrases.example: 두 사람의 설명은 서로 모순되지 않아요.
phrases.en: The two explanations do not contradict each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 말이 서로 맞는다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says that two things are consistent.

explain_en: Use it when words, thoughts or actions do not fit each other. The noun '모순' is also common, as in '모순이 있다' or '모순이 생기다'. Each part may seem right alone but they clash together, and you can say '앞뒤가 안 맞다' instead.

examples.ko: 그 가게의 불친절한 태도는 손님들의 빈축을 샀어요.
examples.en: The shop's unfriendly attitude drew customers' disapproval.

examples.ko: 정치인의 막말이 국민의 빈축을 사고 있어요.
examples.en: The politician's harsh remarks are drawing public disapproval.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 휴대폰을 보면 빈축을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you look at your phone during a meeting, you may get frowned upon.
I was careful with my words so as not to get disapproving looks.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에 시끄럽게 해서 친구들의 빈축을 샀어요.
examples.en: I made noise during exam week and earned my friends' disapproval.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 사과문은 오히려 더 큰 빈축을 샀어요.
examples.en: The company's apology actually drew even greater disapproval.

explain: 거의 '빈축을 사다' 꼴로만 쓰고, 행동이나 말 때문에 사람들이 눈살을 찌푸리게 된다는 뜻이에요. 비슷한 표현으로 '눈총을 받다', '비난을 받다'가 있고, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 공공장소에서 큰 소리로 떠들면 빈축을 사요.
phrases.en: If you talk loudly in a public place, people will frown on you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사다'는 물건을 사는 게 아니라 좋지 않은 반응을 스스로 불러온다는 뜻이에요. 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here '사다' does not mean buying; it means bringing disapproval on yourself. It is fairly formal and common in news and writing.

explain_en: It is used almost only in the form '빈축을 사다', meaning people frown on you because of your actions or words. Similar expressions are '눈총을 받다' and '비난을 받다', and it appears often in the news.

examples.en: You need practice in thinking logically.
He is a person who thinks about problems differently.
If you think deeply, the answer shows up.
Children think while they play.
When I thought flexibly, a solution came to mind.
Gather information before you reason it through.

explain: '생각하다'는 일상 말이고, '사고하다'는 논리적으로 따져 생각한다는 딱딱한 글말이에요. 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 '사고력', '창의적으로 사고하다'처럼 교육·논문에서 자주 나와요. 소리가 같은 '사고(事故, accident)'와 구별하세요.

phrases.en: There are many students who think creatively.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about education.

phrases.en: Reading books improves your thinking ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사고하다'에서 나온 말로, 생각하는 힘을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Comes from 사고하다 and means the power to think.

phrases.en: Think deeply before you answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '사고하다' 대신 '생각하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation, use 생각하다 instead of 사고하다.

explain_en: '생각하다' is everyday; '사고하다' is a stiff written word for reasoning logically. It's rare in conversation and shows up in education and papers, like '사고력'. Don't mix it up with the same-sounding '사고' (accident).

examples.en: You brought an umbrella ahead of time, what foresight!

examples.ko: 그때 집을 사 둔 건 정말 선견지명이었어요.
examples.en: Buying the house back then was truly a wise move.
He had foresight, so his investment succeeded.

examples.ko: 선견지명이 없었다면 큰 손해를 봤을 거예요.
examples.en: Without that foresight, we would have suffered a big loss.

examples.ko: 사장님의 선견지명 덕분에 회사가 위기를 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the boss's foresight, the company got through the crisis.

examples.ko: 저는 선견지명이 부족해서 늘 준비가 늦어요.
examples.en: I lack foresight, so I'm always late preparing.

explain: 보통 '선견지명이 있다/없다'로 쓰고, 미리 준비한 일이 잘됐을 때 '선견지명이네요'라고 칭찬해요. 우산을 챙기는 것 같은 작은 일에도 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 선견지명이 있어서 미리 준비했어요.
phrases.en: He had foresight, so he prepared in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞일을 미리 내다보는 능력이 있다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment that someone can see ahead.

phrases.example: 저는 선견지명이 없어서 늘 늦게 준비해요.
phrases.en: I have no foresight, so I always prepare late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 대비하지 못했을 때 아쉬움을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses regret about not preparing ahead.

phrases.en: That investor is famous for his excellent foresight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이 매우 좋다고 높이 평가하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong praise of someone's ability.

explain_en: It is usually used as '선견지명이 있다/없다', and you praise someone with '선견지명이네요' when their early preparation paid off. You can use it lightly even for small things like bringing an umbrella.

examples.ko: 첫인상 때문에 선입관을 갖지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: I try not to form preconceptions because of first impressions.
Try eating it once without any preconceptions.
My preconception about that person was broken.

examples.ko: 외모만 보고 선입관을 가지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't form preconceptions just by looking at appearance.
I missed a good chance because of my preconception.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 선입관과 달리 정말 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Unlike what I assumed, that movie was really fun.

explain: '편견'은 한쪽으로 치우친 나쁜 생각에 가깝고, '선입관'은 직접 겪기 전에 미리 가진 생각이라 좋은 쪽일 수도 있어요. '선입견'이라고도 하고, '선입관을 갖다/버리다/깨다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I misunderstood that person because of a preconception.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선입관'과 거의 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 선입관; both are widely used.

phrases.example: 처음 보는 음식에 선입관을 갖지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't have preconceptions about food you see for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 정해 둔 생각이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you already have a fixed idea.

phrases.en: If you drop your preconceptions, you can see new things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 가진 생각을 내려놓는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to put aside what you assumed beforehand.

explain_en: '편견' leans toward a biased, negative view, while '선입관' is an idea formed before experiencing something, which can even be positive. It is also said '선입견', and used as '선입관을 갖다/버리다/깨다'.

examples.en: I want to hold on to even the faintest hope to the end.
The chance of rescue was slim as a thread, so everyone was worried.
The faint expectation finally became reality.
His voice sounded as thin as a thread.
The odds of winning are slim, but I'll give it a try.
I didn't give up even when the possibility was extremely slim.

explain: '희망', '가능성', '목숨'처럼 거의 사라질 듯 아주 약하게 남은 것과 함께 써요. '실낱같은 희망'이라는 덩어리로 외워 두면 편해요.

phrases.en: His life hung by a thread, but we didn't give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 사라질 듯 아주 약한 생명을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a life so weak that it may fade at any moment.
phrases.en_equiv: a life hanging by a thread

phrases.en: A slim chance still remains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성공할 확률이 거의 없지만 완전히 없는 것은 아닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the chance is tiny but not completely gone.

phrases.en: Our chance of winning is very slim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 끝내서 상황을 바로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite ending for stating the situation directly.

explain_en: It goes with things barely left, such as '희망' (hope), '가능성' (possibility) and '목숨' (life). It is easy to remember as the chunk '실낱같은 희망'.

en: to be related; to be connected

examples.ko: 이 사건은 지난달 일과 연관돼 있어요.
examples.en: This incident is connected to last month's event.
Health and sleep are deeply related.
I called in everyone involved and talked.
I don't want to be involved in that matter.
Check whether the two problems are connected.

examples.ko: 주제와 연관되지 않은 이야기는 빼 주세요.
examples.en: Please leave out stories unrelated to the topic.

explain: '관련되다'와 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 조사는 '~와/과 연관되다'를 써요. 사건이나 사람이 어떤 일에 얽혀 있을 때도 쓰고, 이 경우에는 조금 부정적인 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '관련이 있다'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: This problem is related to the environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연관되다'와 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 조금 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '연관되다' and interchangeable, but a bit more everyday.

phrases.en: The two things are connected to each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연관되다'를 '~이 있다'로 풀어서 말하는 쉬운 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say it, using '~이 있다' instead of the verb form.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 그 사건과 연관되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That person was not connected to the incident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 얽히지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone was not involved in something.

explain_en: Nearly interchangeable with '관련되다'. The pattern is '~와/과 연관되다'. When a person or event is tied up in some matter it can sound a bit negative. In daily talk '관련이 있다' is more common.

dis.h: linked in a chain of connection

p.n: Almost the same; 관련되다 is more general.

en: to be worried; to be depressed

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 후로 그는 계속 침울해요.
examples.en: Ever since failing the exam, he has been gloomy.
My friend's expression looks gloomy today.
The meeting ended in a gloomy atmosphere.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 마음이 침울해지곤 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, my mood often turns gloomy.
Why are you sitting there looking so down?
My gloomy mood lifted thanks to my friend.

explain: '우울하다'는 마음 상태 전체에 쓰고, '침울하다'는 표정, 분위기, 목소리에 기운 없는 모습이 드러날 때 자주 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 '분위기'에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: He came in with a gloomy expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기운 없는 얼굴이 보일 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for a face that looks low in energy.

phrases.example: 소식을 들은 뒤 방 안이 침울한 분위기였어요.
phrases.en: After hearing the news, the mood in the room was gloomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 한 명이 아니라 모임이나 장소 전체의 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the mood of a whole group or place, not just one person.

phrases.en: My friend has been feeling down for several days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 침울해하는 모습을 밖에서 보고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when describing someone else's gloomy state as you observe it.

explain_en: '우울하다' covers the overall state of mind, while '침울하다' is often used when low spirits show in a face, atmosphere or voice. It can describe not only people but also a '분위기' (mood).

examples.en: Don't rationalize your mistake; apologize first.
That's just rationalizing your laziness.

examples.ko: 자기 합리화가 심한 사람과는 대화하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to talk with someone who rationalizes their own actions a lot.

examples.ko: 회사는 업무 절차 합리화를 추진하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is pushing to make its work procedures more rational.

examples.ko: 변명처럼 들리는 합리화는 누구나 해 본 적 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has made rationalizations that sound like excuses.

examples.ko: 그 선택을 합리화할 이유를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a reason to justify that choice.

explain: 일상에서는 '자기 합리화'라는 말로 자주 써서, 잘못을 그럴듯한 이유로 덮는 안 좋은 느낌이 있어요. 반면 회사나 제도 이야기에서는 '절차를 합리화하다'처럼 더 효율적으로 바꾼다는 중립적인 뜻으로도 써요. 앞에 오는 말을 보고 구별해요.

phrases.en: That's nothing but self-justification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신의 잘못을 그럴듯하게 설명할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for explaining away one's own fault.

phrases.en: Don't rationalize your own actions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 잘못에 이유를 붙인다는 부정적인 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb it often has a negative feeling of making excuses.

phrases.en: The company made its work procedures more efficient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제도나 방법을 더 효율적으로 바꾼다는 중립적인 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral meaning of making a system or method more efficient.

explain_en: In daily talk it often appears as '자기 합리화' and has a negative feel of covering a fault with a plausible reason. In talk about companies or systems, as in '절차를 합리화하다', it is neutral and means making something more efficient. Look at the word before it to tell which one is meant.
